titel: Too $hort Talks Blow the Whistle, Working with Biggie & Tupac and New Album "Sir Too $hort, Vol. 2"

einzeiler: Hip-hop legend Too $hort discusses his iconic career, new music, and early days in…
kurzfassung: Hip-hop pioneer Too $hort reflects on his legendary career, from selling custom cassette tapes to drug dealers in Oakland to releasing multi-platinum albums. He discusses the creative process behind his timeless hits like "Blow the Whistle" and collaborating with icons like Tupac and Biggie. The conversation also covers his new four-part project, "Sir Too $hort, Vol. 2," and his enduring legacy in rap.
stichpunkte: Too $hort started his career by selling custom rap cassette tapes directly to drug dealers in Oakland during the early 1980s.
His high school nickname became his lifelong moniker, eventually evolving into the title of his latest album series, "Sir Too $hort, Vol. 2."
He achieved six consecutive platinum albums before staging a heavily publicized retirement stunt in 1996.
Working with Lil Jon led to the creation of generational hits like "Blow the Whistle," which continues to resonate globally.
He shares behind-the-scenes stories of recording with hip-hop greats like The Notorious B.I.G. and Tupac Shakur.
He is part of the first generation of senior citizen rappers who continue to actively perform and tour.
He recorded roughly 50 songs with Mount Westmore during the COVID-19 pandemic.
He reflects on the evolution of hip-hop, the shift from regional scenes to digital immediacy, and the importance of artist development.

kapitel.titel: Early Days and Selling Tapes in Oakland
The Evolution of Rap and the "Player" Lifestyle
Collaborations with Biggie, Tupac, and Jay-Z
The Making of "Blow the Whistle" and New Music

clips.hook: Selling tapes to drug dealers for $20
clips.text: After bringing a personalized rap tape to a local street boss, the artist received a twenty-dollar bill instead of the usual five-dollar price, inspiring a lucrative business model.

clips.hook: The retirement stunt that boosted sales
clips.text: A staged press conference announcing his retirement provided unprecedented free promotion for his album, driving sales up significantly.
The Notorious B.I.G. walked into the booth and delivered an iconic verse instantly without writing down a single word on paper.
The rapper reveals that he did not reach his adult height until the summer following his nineteenth birthday.
The entire Bay Area community can vouch that the artist was recording extremely explicit rap rhymes as early as the start of the 1980s.

beschreibung:
Too $hort joins us to look back on more than four decades in hip-hop and the stories behind one of the genre’s most enduring careers. He takes us back to Oakland in the ’80s, when he was selling $20 custom raps on cassette to local drug dealers, and explains how his voice and name became famous around the Bay Area before people even knew what he looked like. He also gets into the stories behind songs like “Freaky Tales” and “Blowjob Betty,” his mother’s reaction to his music, the meaning of being a “player,” and why his supposed retirement in 1996 was never quite what it seemed.

Now 60 years old and still going strong, he breaks down his place in hip-hop history, from the ’90s East Coast–West Coast rivalry and the rise of hyphy to the Lil Jon collaboration that changed the course of his career and the making of “Blow the Whistle.” Too $hort shares what it was like recording with The Notorious B.I.G., Tupac and JAY-Z (the only rapper to do so!), including watching Biggie work without writing down his verses and the incredible speed of Tupac’s process. Plus, he talks working with Snow Tha Product, forming Mount Westmore with Snoop Dogg, Ice Cube and E-40, becoming a father later in life, and so much more.
